small_guidance:
- Add a few larger-K autotune configs (e.g. BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=128, num_warps=8, num_stages=3) and a BLOCK_M=64/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64 variant — at K=8192 a deeper K tile reduces loop overhead and increases MAC density.
- Drop `eviction_policy='evict_first'` on the A/B loads; with N=8192 the B tiles are reused across M tiles within a GROUP_M swizzle, so default LRU is better. Keep `evict_last` on the bias only.
- Since M, N, K are all multiples of 256, add a `EVEN_K`/no-mask fast path (skip masks on a/b loads) and use `tl.multiple_of`/`tl.max_contiguous` hints on offs to enable wider vectorized loads.
large_guidance:
- Convert to a persistent / split-K aware GEMM: launch one program per SM (128 SMs-equivalent grid on 4090) and stream tiles, which removes launch-tail imbalance for the 2048×8192×8192 shape and improves L2 reuse of the WT matrix across consecutive output tiles.
- Store weights pre-transposed once in `__init__` (and optionally in fp16/bf16 with an fp32 accumulator) to halve DRAM traffic on the dominant B-matrix load; the GEMM is bandwidth-bound at this size on a 4090 (~1 TB/s), so reducing weight bytes is the biggest lever.
- Consider a TMA-style double-buffered pipeline with `num_stages=4` and `BLOCK_K=128`, plus an explicit `tl.dot` accumulator in fp32 with TF32 inputs; fuse the bias+scale+hardtanh+GELU epilogue exactly as today (already optimal).
